Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClinicWise: dataflow & prompt/output retention — post-call recap

Hi Sarah / Derek,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. I wanted to capture the follow-ups we agreed on and the handful of clarifying questions from your security and engineering teams so we can close the qualification checklist for Demo -> Pilot.

Quick recap of asks we logged on the call:
- Confirmation of what prompt inputs and generated outputs (both streamed and final) you consider "PII" for ClinicWise. You mentioned patient names, MRNs, and free-text clinical notes.
- Residency constraint: production inference must run only in us-east-1.
- Logging requirements: audit logs for admin activity, and per-request telemetry for 12 months.
- Retention windows: you asked for proposed retention defaults and options for shorter TTLs.
- Evidence: a short diagram of our dataflow and a one-pager we can hand to your security folks.

Action items I took away:
1) I will send a concise note confirming how Redwood treats prompt inputs and outputs by default and the options we can offer for stricter retention.
2) Internal ask: loop in Product/Privacy to confirm the retention/role-based access knobs and how we document them in the contract addendum.

Attachments: clinicwise-pii-handling-notes.pdf (summary), redwood-dataflow-diagram.png

Proposed next steps:
- I'll follow up with a technical note by EOD tomorrow (Thu) that lists default retention, encryption, and residency specifics.
- If that matches, we can schedule a short security review with your InfoSec next week.

Rachel

From: Sarah Mills <sarah@clinicwise.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClinicWise: dataflow & prompt/output retention — post-call recap

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our InfoSec side:
- PII scope: patient names, DOB, MRN, and any free-text clinical notes are in-scope. We treat IDs and provider names as non-sensitive for this integration, but we'd prefer to err on the side of caution.
- Residency: yes, inference must execute in us-east-1 only.
- Retention: our baseline requirement is that prompt inputs are kept no longer than 30 days unless explicitly approved; generated outputs used for QA/triage can be kept up to 90 days, but we want the option to set a shorter TTL per environment.
- Audit logs: 365 days for admin/audit logs (who changed configs, who accessed logs).
- Encryption: all data at rest must be customer-keyed (KMS).

We appreciate the diagram and the one-pager. Please include the explicit retention windows in your note and call out the ability to disable output persistence entirely — that's a hard requirement for some of our workflows.

Happy to take a 30-min InfoSec call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ClinicWise: dataflow & prompt/output retention — post-call recap

Team — forwarding ClinicWise answers and InfoSec asks. TL;DR of their constraints:
- Residency: us-east-1 only.
- Prompt inputs TTL <= 30 days by default; outputs TTL up to 90 days but must be configurable down to 0 (no persistence).
- 365-day audit log retention.
- Customer KMS for at-rest encryption.

Questions for Product/Privacy:
1) Can we support per-environment TTLs and an explicit "zero-persistence" mode for outputs? If yes, any caveats for streaming responses / KV cache?
2) Is customer-managed KMS already supported for Dedicated and Private customers? What about Hosted customers (Hub-layer KMS + CMK wrapping)?
3) For audit log retention, do we have a straightforward policy/contract clause and evidence we can share (example log retention table + sample sanitized log)?

I attached the diagram and the summary PDF that I intend to send to their InfoSec once we confirm the TTL/KMS answers. Can y'all weigh in by EOD so I can get back to ClinicWise and lock their security review call for next week?

Thanks — Rachel

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ClinicWise: dataflow & prompt/output retention — post-call recap

Rachel / Grace,

Quick answers from infra/product privacy:
- Per-environment TTLs: supported in Redwood Dedicated and Private now; Hosted customers can request TTL overrides via account config, and we can enforce shorter retention with an S3 lifecycle + retention flag. For "zero-persistence" mode: we can implement ephemeral outputs by disabling disk-backed persistence and ensuring KV cache is not checkpointed to durable storage — caveat: this increases cold-start probability for repeated prompts.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers: we offer envelope encryption where customer provides a CMK and we wrap keys on their behalf (we will outline this in the one-pager).
- Audit logs: we maintain admin/audit logs 365 days by default for Dedicated and Hosted (configurable for enterprise contracts). We can provide a sanitized sample and the table for the contract addendum.

I confirm the attached dataflow diagram aligns with how requests traverse the runtime (routing -> serving -> ephemeral KV -> telemetry sink). Happy to join the InfoSec call if needed.

Aditya Rao
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
